title: Quasi-compact Deligne--Mumford stacks admit affine smooth presentations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use its field-valued point space $|\mathcal X|$ and atlas topology as in [lem-sfb-stack-topology-open-substacks]. Call $\mathcal X$ quasi-compact when every open covering of $|\mathcal X|$ has a finite subcover. The following are equivalent: (1) $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact; (2) there is an affine $S$-scheme $A$ and a representable smooth surjective morphism $A\to\mathcal X$; (3) there is a quasi-compact $S$-scheme $U$ and a representable smooth surjective morphism $U\to\mathcal X$; (4) there is a quasi-compact Deligne--Mumford stack $\mathcal V$ and a surjective morphism $\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$. Here affine means isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a commutative ring $R$, and quasi-compact for a scheme means quasi-compactness of its usual topological space. Smooth representable means that each scheme base change is a smooth map of algebraic spaces, tested on etale scheme charts using [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Surjective means surjective on field-valued point classes. No finite-type, field-base, separatedness or quasi-separatedness assumption is imposed, and the empty stack is allowed.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), conditions (1), (2), (3), (5), restricted to Deligne--Mumford stacks.

proof.text: Assume (1). Choose a representable etale surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$ from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Choose an affine open cover $U_i\hookrightarrow U$ by [lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover]. Each inclusion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so $q_i:U_i\to\mathcal X$ is representable etale by composition in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The same calculus makes it smooth, flat and locally of finite presentation. Regarding each $U_i$ as an algebraic space via [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], apply [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]: its image $W_i\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ is open. That node's topology is the topology specified in the statement: the chosen etale atlas is smooth, and both topologies test opens by inverse image along this atlas. Surjectivity of $p$ gives a lift of every field object after a field extension by the chart-test equivalence in the calculus node; hence $|p|$ is surjective. Since the $U_i$ cover $U$, the $W_i$ cover $|\mathcal X|$.

proof.text: Choose a finite set $J$ of these indices whose $W_j$ cover $|\mathcal X|$, using (1). Form $A=\coprod_{j\in J}U_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The etale maps $q_j$ glue to a representable etale map $q:A\to\mathcal X$ by the coproduct clause of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; that clause also makes it smooth. Its image contains every $W_j$, so it is surjective in the field-point convention specified in the statement. Write $U_j\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $A\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{j\in J}R_j)$, hence $A$ is affine. Its map to $S$ is the one induced by the component maps, and $q$ is over $S$. This proves (2). All coproducts are finite and lie in the standing universe. If the selected set is empty, its spectrum is that of the zero ring and its point image covers precisely when $\mathcal X$ has no points; the empty scheme and its empty map give the required atlas.

proof.text: The affine scheme $A$ in (2) is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Keeping its representable smooth surjection proves (3).

Given (3), regard $U$ as its representable discrete fibred groupoid. This is a Deligne--Mumford stack in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] represent the base changes of its diagonal, and its identity is a surjective etale atlas (the identity is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]). The representable sheaf $h_U$ is an algebraic space with its identity etale atlas by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. A sheaf of sets, regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid, is a stack: a descent datum is a family of sections agreeing on overlaps, and the sheaf axiom gives its unique glued section; all arrows are identities. By [lem-sfb-stack-topology-open-substacks], its point space is the usual space of $U$. Thus $U$, with its given morphism to $\mathcal X$, is a quasi-compact Deligne--Mumford stack as required in (4).

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), scheme-source case of the immediate implications to (5)

proof.text: Given (4), the map $|\mathcal V|\to|\mathcal X|$ is continuous by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]; its topology agrees with the atlas topology specified in the statement as in step 1. It is surjective by the hypothesis of (4). Pull any open cover of $|\mathcal X|$ back to $|\mathcal V|$. Quasi-compactness of $\mathcal V$ selects finitely many inverse images covering $|\mathcal V|$. The corresponding finitely many opens cover $|\mathcal X|$: lift any point to $|\mathcal V|$ and use the finite cover there. This proves (1), and closes the cycle (1) implies (2) implies (3) implies (4) implies (1). No separation assumption on either point space is used.
